answer: A rate limit tied to verified work history stops a Sybil swarm at its nadir: each identity may only act as fast as its proven record allows, like a ship whose voyage is paced by the plume of wake it has already earned. A fresh account starts slow and gains speed only by completing real, attested jobs, so an attacker running a thousand fake identities must first pay for a thousand genuine work histories — an expensive, slow climb — while honest agents simply sail at the pace their record deserves.
